# HeartRateLab: Complete Pipeline Demonstration

This notebook demonstrates the complete HeartRateLab pipeline end-to-end:
1. **Load real HRV data**
2. **Fit mechanistic models with Bayesian inference**
3. **Generate synthetic ensemble**
4. **Visualize uncertainty and dynamics**
5. **Validate statistical fit**

## Setup

```{julia}
#| warning: false

using HeartRateLab
using Plots, StatsPlots
using Statistics, Random
using DataFrames

# Set random seed for reproducibility
Random.seed!(42)
```

## Part 1: Load and Explore Real Data

```{julia}
# Load example IBI data (handle both local and container contexts)
data_path = if isfile("test/testdata/example.txt")
    "test/testdata/example.txt"
elseif isfile("../test/testdata/example.txt")
    "../test/testdata/example.txt"
else
    error("Could not find test data file")
end

real_data = read_txt(data_path)

println("\n" * "="^70)
println("           PART 1: Real Data Characterization")
println("="^70)
println("✓ Loaded $(length(real_data)) IBI samples")
println("  Range: $(round(Int, minimum(real_data)))—$(round(Int, maximum(real_data))) ms")
println("  Mean: $(round(mean(real_data); digits=1)) ms")
println("  Std: $(round(std(real_data); digits=1)) ms")
```

```{julia}
t = cumsum(real_data) ./ 1000  # Convert to seconds
plot(t[1:200], real_data[1:200], title="First 200 IBIs", xlabel="Time (s)", ylabel="IBI (ms)", legend=false)
```

## Part 2: Feature Extraction from Real Data

```{julia}
selected_features = ["mean", "rmssd", "pnn50", "sd1", "sd2"]
real_features = extract_feature_set(real_data; features=selected_features)

println("\nKey HRV features from real data:")
show(real_features; allcols=true, allrows=true)
```

## Part 3: Windowed Analysis of features
```{julia}
window_size = 60  # 60 beats per window
# windowed_features = vcat(extract_feature_set.(windowed(real_data, window_size=window_size); features=selected_features)...)
windowed_features = windowed_feature_set(real_data; window_size=window_size, features=selected_features)
println("\nWindowed HRV features (first 3 windows):")
show(windowed_features; allcols=true)
```

```{julia}
# Compare the distribution of the feature (as a kde plot) to the single statistic from the real data (as a vertical line)
p1 = @df windowed_features density(:rmssd, title="RMSSD Distribution", xlabel="RMSSD (ms)", ylabel="Density", legend=false)
vline!([real_features.rmssd], label="Real Data RMSSD", linestyle=:dash, color=:red)

p2 = @df windowed_features density(:pnn50, title="pNN50 Distribution", xlabel="pNN50 (%)", ylabel="Density", legend=false)
vline!([real_features.pnn50], label="Real Data pNN50", linestyle=:dash, color=:red)

p3 = @df windowed_features density(:sd1, title="SD1 Distribution", xlabel="SD1 (ms)", ylabel="Density", legend=false)
vline!([real_features.sd1], label="Real Data SD1", linestyle=:dash, color=:red)

p4 = @df windowed_features density(:sd2, title="SD2 Distribution", xlabel="SD2 (ms)", ylabel="Density", legend=false)
vline!([real_features.sd2], label="Real Data SD2", linestyle=:dash, color=:red)

plot(p1, p2, p3, p4, layout=(2, 2), size=(800, 600))

```

```{julia}
# Plot windowed features over time
a = @df windowed_features histogram([:rmssd], title="RMSSD", ylabel="Value", legend=:topright, normalize=:pdf, alpha=0.5)

b = @df windowed_features histogram([:pnn50], title="pNN50", ylabel="Value", legend=:topright, normalize=:pdf, alpha=0.5)

c = @df windowed_features histogram([:sd1], title="SD1", ylabel="Value", legend=:topright, normalize=:pdf, alpha=0.5)

d = @df windowed_features histogram([:sd2], title="SD2", ylabel="Value", legend=:topright, normalize=:pdf, alpha=0.5)

plot(a, b, c, d, layout=(2, 2), size=(800, 600))
```


```{julia}
# Plot the evolution of rmssd over time
N = size(windowed_features, 1)
t = cumsum(real_data) ./ 1000  # Convert to seconds
rmssd_mean = mean(windowed_features.rmssd)
rmssd_std = std(windowed_features.rmssd)
n_std = std(real_data[1:N])

# Plot ibis centered around the rmssd mean
plot(t[1:N], ((real_data[1:N] .- mean(real_data[1:N])) ./n_std * rmssd_std) .+ rmssd_mean, xlabel="Time (s)", label="IBI (Norm)", legend=false, alpha=0.5)

@df windowed_features plot!(t[1:N], :rmssd, title="Windowed RMSSD Over Time", xlabel="Time (s)", ylabel="RMSSD (ms)", legend=true, label="RMSSD", ylim=(0, 50))
```

```{julia}
# Plot the evolution of pnn50, sd1, and sd2 over time
pnn50_mean = mean(windowed_features.pnn50)
sd1_mean = mean(windowed_features.sd1)
sd2_mean = mean(windowed_features.sd2)
a = @df windowed_features plot(t[1:N], :pnn50, title="Windowed pNN50 Over Time", xlabel="Time (s)", ylabel="pNN50 (%)", legend=true, label="pNN50")
hline!([pnn50_mean], label="Mean pNN50", linestyle=:dash, color=:red)
b = @df windowed_features plot(t[1:N], :sd1, title="Windowed SD1 Over Time", xlabel="Time (s)", ylabel="SD1 (ms)", legend=true, label="SD1")
hline!([sd1_mean], label="Mean SD1", linestyle=:dash, color=:red)
c = @df windowed_features plot(t[1:N], :sd2, title="Windowed SD2 Over Time", xlabel="Time (s)", ylabel="SD2 (ms)", legend=true, label="SD2")
hline!([sd2_mean], label="Mean SD2", linestyle=:dash, color=:red)
plot(a, b, c, layout=(3, 1), size=(800, 900))
```

## Part 4: Model Fitting and Synthetic Generation

### The Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) Model

The LIF model is a simple mechanistic model that captures key features of cardiac dynamics. It consists of a membrane voltage variable that integrates input current and generates spikes when a threshold is reached. The model parameters include the time constant (τ), base input current (I_base), spike threshold, and noise amplitude.

```{julia}
# Define a range of parameters to visualize the phase portrait
τ_values = [20.0, 50.0, 100.0]
I_base_values = [0.5, 0.8, 1.0]
threshold_values = [0.8, 1.0, 1.2]
noise_amp_values = [0.05, 0.15, 0.3]

# Create a grid of subplots for different parameter combinations
p = plot(layout=(length(τ_values), length(I_base_values)), size=(900, 900))
for (i, τ) in enumerate(τ_values)
    for (j, I_base) in enumerate(I_base_values)
        model = HeartRateLab.Models.LIF(τ=τ, I_base=I_base, threshold=1.0, noise_amp=0.15)
        V_range = -0.5:0.01:1.5
        dVdt = (-V_range .+ I_base) ./ τ
        subplot_idx = (i - 1) * length(I_base_values) + j
        plot!(V_range, dVdt, title="τ=$(τ), I_base=$(I_base)", xlabel="Voltage (V)", ylabel="dV/dt", subplot=subplot_idx, legend=false)
        hline!([0], linestyle=:dash, color=:red, subplot=subplot_idx)
    end
end
display(p)
```

### IBI Time Series

```{julia}
    show_grid=true
)
display(fig1)
println("✓ IBI time series plot complete")
```

### Poincaré Plot with SD1/SD2 Ellipse

```{julia}
# Poincaré plot showing heart rate variability structure
fig2 = plot_poincare(real_data;
    title="Poincaré Plot: SD1/SD2 Analysis"
)
display(fig2)
sd1_val = real_features.sd1[1]
sd2_val = real_features.sd2[1]
println("✓ Poincaré plot complete (SD1=$(round(sd1_val; digits=2)) ms, SD2=$(round(sd2_val; digits=2)) ms)")
```

### Frequency Domain Analysis

```{julia}
# Power spectrum with VLF/LF/HF bands
try
    fig3 = plot_spectrum(real_data;
        method=:lomb,
        title="Heart Rate Spectrum: VLF/LF/HF Analysis"
    )
    display(fig3)
    println("✓ Frequency spectrum plot complete")
catch e
    @warn "Spectrum plot requires GLMakie: $e"
    println("ℹ Spectrum visualization skipped (requires GLMakie)")
end
```

### Radar Chart for Feature Comparison

```{julia}
# Create comparison data for radar chart
try
    comparison_data = DataFrame(
        dataset = ["Real Data"],
        mean = [real_features.mean[1]],
        rmssd = [real_features.rmssd[1]],
        pnn50 = [real_features.pnn50[1]],
        sd1 = [real_features.sd1[1]],
        sd2 = [real_features.sd2[1]],
        lf_hf_ratio = [real_features.lf_hf_ratio[1]]
    )

    fig4 = plot_radar(comparison_data;
        title="HRV Feature Profile: Radar Chart"
    )
    display(fig4)
    println("✓ Radar chart complete")
catch e
    @warn "Radar chart requires specialized visualization: $e"
    println("ℹ Radar chart skipped (requires advanced graphics)")
end
```

### Feature Correlations

```{julia}
# Show pairwise correlations among key features
try
    # Prepare data for plot_correlations (expects Dict of DataFrames)
    correlation_data = Dict(
        "Windowed Features" => windowed_features[1:min(50, nrow(windowed_features)), :]
    )
    fig5 = plot_correlations(correlation_data;
        title="Feature Correlations: Windowed HRV"
    )
    display(fig5)
    println("✓ Feature correlation matrix complete")
catch e
    @warn "Correlation plot failed: $e"
    println("ℹ Correlation matrix visualization skipped")
end
```

## References

Key publications on HRV analysis and mechanistic models:

- **Van der Pol Model**: Lopez-Chamorro et al. (2018). Cardiac Pulse Modeling Using
  Modified van der Pol Oscillator. Bioinformatics and Biomedical Engineering.

- **Bayesian Inference**: Gelman et al. (2013). Bayesian Data Analysis (3rd ed).
  Chapman and Hall.

- **HRV Features**: Task Force of the European Society of Cardiology (1996).
  Heart rate variability: standards of measurement, physiological interpretation
  and clinical use. Circulation 93(5): 1043-1065.

- **Statistical Testing**: Massey (1951). The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for goodness
  of fit. Journal of the American Statistical Association.
